features.evidence: scale scarce security judgment
features.name: Security automation mission fit
features.description: Captures how well the letter shows understanding of and motivation for the role's core mission of automating security workflows at scale.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in Google, software, or security with little connection to the team's automation mandate.
Expresses interest in security impact or company scale but links it only loosely to the actual work of the role.
Clearly ties personal goals to automating security workflows, vulnerability response, or developer-facing tooling.
Shows a nuanced understanding of security automation as a leverage problem and makes it a central career motivation.

features.evidence: inherited by every team downstream
features.name: Foundational systems orientation
features.description: Captures whether the applicant is drawn to platform work whose benefits compound across many teams and services.

levels.descriptor: Focuses mainly on generic software work or a single product, with no clear platform orientation.
Mentions broad organizational impact or scale only in passing.
Explicitly values foundational or central tooling whose benefits spread across many teams.
Makes platform leverage a defining theme and links prior work or desired impact to compounding downstream benefits.

features.evidence: make the secure path the easy path
features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security work as enabling developers through defaults, tooling, and proactive assistance rather than policing.

levels.descriptor: Does not show a clear philosophy of helping developers through security tooling or defaults.
Hints at supporting engineers or being proactive rather than reactive, but only briefly.
Explicitly frames security as enabling developers via good defaults, practical tooling, or proactive assistance.

features.evidence: Doctoral degree in computer science
features.name: Advanced academic qualification
features.description: Captures the highest formal CS-related degree or equivalent preparation presented in the letter.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
Master's degree in a relevant field.
Doctoral degree or PhD in a relevant field.

features.evidence: 7 years at Expedia
features.name: Relevant software tenure
features.description: Captures the amount of professional software experience the applicant presents in testing, maintaining, or launching products.

levels.descriptor: Roughly meets the minimum bar, with about 2 to 3 years of relevant professional experience.
Shows solid mid-level tenure, with about 4 to 5 years of relevant experience.
Shows more extensive tenure, with about 6 or more years of relevant experience.

features.evidence: launching 6 production services

features.description: Captures the breadth of concrete production-service experience described, especially launch and maintenance of real systems.

levels.descriptor: Mentions only limited production exposure or one to two services.
Describes several production systems, typically three to four, or moderate ownership across launch and maintenance.
Shows broad production experience, such as five or more services and or clear end-to-end responsibility.

features.evidence: production-grade, not just scripting

features.description: Captures how substantial the candidate's Python experience appears, from lightweight scripting to production services and tooling others rely on.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or mentioned only as basic familiarity.
Uses Python regularly for scripts, prototypes, or routine internal tools.
Shows substantial Python responsibility in production services or important internal tooling.
Demonstrates production-grade Python practice, such as typed or tested code, extensible services, or tooling other engineers depend on.

features.evidence: classified, deduplicated, and attached to the right owner
features.name: Vulnerability handling automation
features.description: Captures direct experience automating vulnerability intake, classification, routing, deduplication, or related response workflows.

levels.descriptor: No direct vulnerability-handling automation experience is described.
Claims relevant automation experience, but only in general terms.
Describes a concrete triage pipeline or workflow with recognizable steps such as intake, classification, routing, or deduplication.
Describes concrete vulnerability-handling automation and also states a clear operational effect such as reduced manual work, faster routing, or recovered expert time.

features.evidence: mapping attack surfaces and validating fixes

features.description: Captures hands-on involvement in assessing systems for security weaknesses and verifying remediation.

levels.descriptor: No direct security assessment work is described.
Mentions security reviews or assessments in generic terms without showing what was done.
Gives concrete assessment activities such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, or validation of fixes.
Shows strong assessment ownership, repeated practice, or an especially credible lens such as reviewing unfamiliar systems like an attacker or a builder.

features.evidence: Python agents plan and act while Go services provide the guardrails

features.description: Captures experience designing agent-based systems with explicit orchestration, boundaries, permissions, or auditability.

levels.descriptor: No agentic or autonomous-system design experience is described.
Mentions agents or automation vaguely, without enough detail to assess architecture.
Describes a concrete agentic setup, typically with Python agents and supporting services or infrastructure.
Shows detailed architecture with permissions, guardrails, logging, auditability, or clear end-to-end design ownership.

features.evidence: evaluation scaffolding required to deploy them responsibly

levels.descriptor: No applied AI or LLM experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI interest or exposure, but not concrete shipped work.
Describes real production AI or LLM-backed features.
Describes production AI work plus reliability practices such as evaluation, hardening, checks, or constraints.

features.evidence: made an intractable dedup problem boringly fast

levels.descriptor: Does not present meaningful evidence of data-structure or algorithmic skill.

Shows especially strong or current applied fluency through multiple examples or a high-impact example on a real bottleneck, hot path, or scaling problem.

features.evidence: typed, tested services and tooling that other engineers extend without fear

levels.descriptor: Provides little evidence of maintainability, testing, safety, or operational care.
Shows some signals of care, such as a maintainer mindset or concern for correctness, but not many concrete practices.

Repeatedly signals high production standards and a habit of building dependable systems with strong constraints and maintainability.

features.evidence: I hold the OSCP certification
features.name: Formal security credential

levels.descriptor: No external security credential is mentioned.
Presents a foundational credential such as Security+ or similar theory-oriented certification.
Presents a hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP or an equivalent lab-based practical assessment.

features.evidence: maintainer of an open-source automation framework with users I have never met

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.

Shows stewardship of a project used by others, with responsibilities such as review, release management, or community maintenance.

features.evidence: built a distributed job scheduler with leader election and crash recovery

levels.descriptor: No side project is mentioned, or the reference is too cursory to add much signal.

features.evidence: measured its worth in the hours of expert attention it returned
